messages:
alice.k: Heads-up — looking at the last 2 hours for the traffic-split experiment (50/50) and the canary slice is showing a drift in tail latency vs baseline. 99p is up ~35%.
ben.t: Ugh. Is that across all endpoints or one route?
carlos_m: just the /generate-paraphrase route. baseline (v2.9) stable. canary (v3.4-quant) spikes under burst traffic.
megan: @alice.k any chance this is sampling bias? did the canary get a different upstream traffic mix?
alice.k: checked headers and user_agent distribution — looks consistent. Request size distribution slightly heavier on canary (median +8% tokens) but not enough to explain 35% 99p.
ryan: deploy-bot: Canary created for model v3.4-quant at 2025-11-02T14:18:41Z :rocket:
ben.t: Could be kernel selection on that HW+quant combo. We should drill into sequence length vs tokenization boundary effects.
carlos_m: Proposed dashboard drilldown: split by seq_len_bucket, client_region, and request_size_percentile. Also show per-variant KV-hit-rate and batching window.
megan: +1. Also add a column for inferred batching latency (time_to_batch_start) — we saw differences earlier between pools.
alice.k: Quick query I used to surface the 99p delta:

```
from metrics
| filter route == "/generate-paraphrase" and rollout_id == "exp-20251102"
| group_by [variant, seq_len_bucket]
| agg p99_latency = quantile(latency_ms, 0.99)
| pivot variant
| calc delta = p99_latency_canary - p99_latency_baseline
| sort desc delta
```

This immediately surfaces the heavy tail on seq_len_bucket >= 512.
ryan: Suggestion: add a temporary guard that reduces canary weight to 10% for sequences >= 512 until we investigate kernel path. We can keep overall 50/50 but route large seqs away.
ben.t: That will change the experiment definition though — we need to record the change and ensure metric comparisons use consistent routing filters.
megan: UX ask for the Console: when a rollout is split by traffic rules, show the effective comparison window and note any differential sampling. Right now the baseline vs canary chart assumes identical input distribution by default which is misleading.
alice.k: Exactly. We should show 'effective sample parity' and a small badge if distributions diverge >5% in key attributes (seq_len, client, model_input_tokens).
carlos_m: For alerting: current canary delta alert fires on absolute p99 change >20ms. For high variance endpoints maybe better to use weighted percent-change normalized by baseline variance (z-score) and require at least N samples.
ben.t: Agree. Proposed new rule: trigger if z_score(delta) > 3 and sample_count_baseline>500 and sample_count_canary>500. Also only for windows with stable traffic (no sudden traffic ramp >20% within window).
ryan: From infra side, I can add a quick guard policy that modifies routing rules: a per-route traffic condition expression like `if seq_len >= 512 then weight_canary = 0.1` — we already support conditional routing in YAML. Example:

```
traffic:
  - variant: canary
    weight: 0.5
    condition: "seq_len >= 512 => weight: 0.1"
  - variant: baseline
    weight: 0.5
```

We should make Console show an explicit preview of effective traffic after conditions are applied.
megan: UX: when previewing a rollout, surface a small table: "effective slice weights" (region x seq_bucket) so product owners can see where their canary is actually exercised.
alice.k: For immediate ops: I'll mute the existing p99 delta alert for this rollout and create a temporary one with z-score logic. @ryan can you implement the conditional traffic tweak and we will rerun the experiment?
ryan: On it. I'll push a patch to routing-service and post link to the PR.
observability-bot: New dashboard card created: "exp-20251102 — seq_len slice view" (link). Auto-updated every 1m.
ben.t: Thanks. Also we should add a note to the rollout record: 'Investigating tail latency increase for seq_len >= 512 on v3.4-quant — possible kernel mismatch / batch packing'.
alice.k: I'll file a short postmortem-style note in the rollout metadata after investigation. If we confirm kernel issue, we can add an automated fallback policy (route large seqs to baseline) for future canaries with similar hardware.
megan: UX follow-up ticket: console should expose a 'slice-aware rollback' button that can apply a conditional revert (eg. revert variants only for affected slices). This avoids full rollback when impact is localized.
carlos_m: +1, very useful.
alice.k: Ok team, next steps: ryan implements conditional weight change; observability-bot card will help validate; megan files Console UX tickets; ben updates alerting rule. We'll reconvene in 30m.
ryan: PR: https://internal/repo/routing-service/pull/482
ben.t: Alert rule draft: alert_exp313_stockholm_latency_zscore.md
megan: Filed UX: CONSOLE-1723 (slice-weight preview + conditional rollback)
alice.k: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
